claims.text: FeCoNiPd is an fcc high-entropy alloy.
FeCoNiPd exhibits low coercivity and soft-ferromagnetic behavior.
The proposed intervention replaces Pd with W in an almost equiatomic FeCoNi-based quaternary alloy.
The proposed almost equiatomic composition has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
The W-substituted alloy can retain a homogeneous, single-phase fcc structure under suitable processing conditions.
Replacing Pd with W enhances local lattice distortion in the FeCoNi-based alloy.
Replacing Pd with W increases spin–orbit coupling in the FeCoNi-based alloy.
W has a higher atomic mass and a size mismatch relative to the other alloying elements.
Stronger spin–orbit coupling and greater local lattice distortion enhance magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The W-induced structural and electronic changes create effective domain-wall pinning centers.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain-wall pinning raise coercivity.
Equiatomic FeCoNiW will have greater coercivity than the FeCoNiPd baseline.
The W-substituted alloy will retain high saturation magnetization.
The predicted coercivity enhancement applies only while the W-substituted alloy remains single-phase fcc.
Phase separation or formation of non-fcc phases may prevent the predicted coercivity enhancement.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the coercivity prediction applies only to a single-phase fcc alloy and may fail after phase separation, whereas the falsification rule treats observation of phase separation or a non-fcc structure as falsifying the hypothesis. Such a specimen is outside the stated applicability conditions, so it cannot by itself decisively falsify the conditional coercivity claim.
